newsitem.title: MEXICO: Left alleges government vote-buying in Mexico vote.
newsitem.headline: Left alleges government vote-buying in Mexico vote.

text.p: Mexico's main left-wing party accused the government on Wednesday of massive vote-buying ahead of local elections in the troubled southwestern state of Guerrero.

More than 1.3 million people in Guerrero, a state which stretches from the glitzy Pacific resort of Acapulco to remote, dangerous and poverty-stricken mountain villages, will elect mayors and local deputies on Sunday.

The ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), which strongly denies accusations of vote-buying, controls 68 of the state's 76 town halls. The PRI hopes to retain power even under fairer electoral rules imposed over the past few years and with a stronger opposition.

The main opposition in the state, the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), accused the PRI of waging a "dirty war" against its candidates despite promises by President Ernesto Zedillo of a fair campaign.

Pablo Gomez, Electoral Action Secretary of the PRD's national executive, told a news conference "cash is sent through federal channels to the state government which distributes it to the party structure."
The money, he added, was sent "on the direct orders of the President of the Republic" and came from a special secret budget reserved for the president's use.

Chief government spokesman Dionisio Perez Jacome said he was "absolutely sure" no federal money was being used to buy votes. "Any diversion of funds is impossible with the strict controls we have nowadays ... it would be detected immediately."
The PRD in a statement also accused the government of inhibiting voters by maintaining a big troop presence in Guerrero ahead of the elections.
The government has said the troops are necessary to guarantee law and order because of the emergence of a new guerrilla group in the state, the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR).
Gomez said allegations of vote-buying and intimidation would produce a climate in which "the response to any kind of aggression against the popular vote could be very strong."
The PRD has said it expects to win 30 towns in Guerrero, among them Acapulco. It currently governs six.
